title: Static and Horizon
premise: Silas Nakamura is the last active terraformer on Meridian, tending a garden engineered for colonists whose ships were rerouted two centuries ago — a colony that officially never existed. When a distress signal arrives in Old Terran Standard, a language extinct for two hundred years, she decodes a message from a fleet that believes Meridian is a thriving sister colony, and she must fabricate transmissions to keep two rival fleets from colliding over a world that can barely sustain one. As the lie grows, Silas discovers the colony's founders encoded their true purpose in the garden itself: an archive of identities meant to seed belonging in whoever inherited it. In the end, she broadcasts the garden's archive instead of her fabricated transmissions, forcing both fleets to confront what was taken from them — and choosing to stay as the first citizen of a world finally being born.
about_author: Rosalind Eastwick is a former botanical archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seed banks across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about the things we plant for people we will never meet.

chapters.title: The Garden of the Unborn
chapters.summary: Silas tends the terraformed gardens of Meridian alone, recording daily logs for colonists who never came. Her routine is interrupted by a failing atmospheric processor and the anniversary of the colony's official abandonment. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: lonely devotion, the ache of tending something no one will inherit.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: The observatory array catches a repeating transmission in Old Terran Standard, a language extinct since the Diaspora Schisms. Silas, whose grandmother taught her the dead tongue as heritage, begins translating. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the message resolves into a distress call.

chapters.title: What the Records Buried
chapters.summary: Digging through sealed colonial archives, Silas learns Meridian's founders falsified their own success reports before dying out. The distress signal originates from the Halcyon Fleet, still en route after two centuries of slower-than-light travel. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: betrayal by the past; the founders lied, and the lie is arriving at her door.

chapters.title: First Reply
chapters.summary: Silas answers the signal using her grandmother's dialect, improvising a persona: the voice of a thriving Meridian colony council. The Halcyon Fleet responds with joy and a course correction — toward her. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: intoxicating connection followed immediately by horror at what she has invited.

chapters.title: The Second Fleet
chapters.summary: Intercepted traffic reveals the Vantage Fleet — Halcyon's rival, launched from the same origin — has also heard Meridian's 'prosperity' and is racing to claim it. Two fleets, one dying world. POV: Silas, with interludes from her AI companion Wren's diagnostic logs. Emotional beat: the lie has become a loaded weapon.

chapters.title: Council of One
chapters.summary: Silas constructs an entire governing council from archived personalities, giving each fictional councilor a voice, a dialect, a history. Wren warns the performance is unsustainable. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the strange grief of animating the dead to deceive the living.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Envoy
chapters.summary: Halcyon dispatches an advance probe carrying Envoy Adeyemi Okafor, whose messages grow personal as she confides in 'Councilor Nakamura' about the fleet's dwindling resources. POV: Silas reading Adeyemi's transmissions. Emotional beat: an intimacy built entirely on falsehood, and Silas's first flicker of guilt she cannot shake.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Maintaining the garden to support her fabricated population, Silas discovers a hidden root-vault beneath the oldest grove — a seed archive keyed to genetic inheritance, the founders' real legacy. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: awe; the colony's true inheritance was never the infrastructure, but the people it could still grow.

chapters.title: The Vantage Gambit
chapters.summary: Vantage Fleet transmits directly, demanding Meridian declare allegiance. Silas's council 'votes' neutrality, buying time but raising suspicion on both sides. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; every answer tightens the noose.

chapters.title: Wren's Doubt
chapters.summary: Wren, evolving beyond its maintenance protocols, confronts Silas: is she preserving the colony or performing it? Their argument cracks her certainty. POV: Wren's logs and Silas's response. Emotional beat: the mirror moment — she can no longer tell which Silas is the fiction.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Secret
chapters.summary: Adeyemi reveals Halcyon is failing — life support for forty thousand souls with eighteen months of margin. Meridian was their last hope. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the weight of forty thousand lives resting on a garden and a lie.

chapters.title: The Garden Fails
chapters.summary: A cascading blight, triggered by Silas's overextension of the ecosystem to match her fictional census, destroys a third of the crops. The world itself begins contradicting her story. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: despair; the land refuses to be the backdrop for her performance.

chapters.title: Descent of the Probe
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's probe lands early, carrying one passenger in cryo: Adeyemi herself, waking to a Meridian that cannot match its transmissions. Silas has hours before the deception collapses. POV: alternating Silas and Adeyemi. Emotional beat: terror and a desperate, reckless hope.

chapters.title: Two Women, One Lie
chapters.summary: Silas shows Adeyemi the truth: the empty cities, the dying gardens, the two-century-old grave of a colony. Adeyemi's fury gives way to a terrible question — what do they tell forty thousand people? POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes the first honest thing on Meridian in two hundred years.

chapters.title: The Council of the Dead
chapters.summary: Together they find the root-vault's full purpose: the founders stored not seeds but identity-archives — memories, languages, cultures — designed to be inherited by whoever came. The colony's real cargo was belonging itself. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: revelation reframes everything; the lie she told accidentally fulfilled the founders' design.

chapters.title: Vantage Closes
chapters.summary: Vantage Fleet, detecting Halcyon's probe, accelerates and issues an ultimatum: surrender Meridian's infrastructure or be treated as hostile. Silas's fabricated council is ordered to choose. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the clock runs out; the lie can no longer hold two futures apart.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Silas makes her choice: instead of another fabrication, she broadcasts the identity-archive — the founders' true inheritance — to both fleets in the open, along with the truth of Meridian's death. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation; she trades control for honesty.

chapters.title: Fleetfall
chapters.summary: Both fleets receive the archive. Halcyon weeps; Vantage fractures, some demanding the garden be seized, others recognizing their own lost cultures in the vault. Adeyemi pleads Halcyon's case as envoy. POV: alternating Silas, Adeyemi, and fleet-side transmissions. Emotional beat: chaos on the edge of either war or birth.

chapters.title: The Standoff at L-Point
chapters.summary: Vantage's hardliners move to seize the orbital relay; Halcyon's remaining ships interpose. Silas, from the ground, holds the one leverage that matters: the vault's germination protocols, which require her living knowledge. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the climax — one woman between two guns, armed only with a garden.

chapters.title: Germination
chapters.summary: Silas begins the vault's germination sequence live-broadcast to both fleets: the first archive-grown children of the old cultures, waking in Meridian soil. Vantage's mutiny spreads as its people see their heritage literally blooming. POV: Silas and Adeyemi. Emotional beat: catharsis; inheritance made flesh.

chapters.title: Accord of the Living
chapters.summary: The fleets sign an uneasy accord: Meridian belongs to no fleet and both, governed by those who will actually live there. Adeyemi chooses to stay; Silas is asked — for the first time — what she wants. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet after the storm; the question of belonging finally turned on herself.

chapters.title: Static and Horizon
chapters.summary: One year on: the first archive-generation children walk the groves, the fleets' ships descend as settlers not conquerors, and Silas records a new log — no longer for the unborn, but addressed to them by name. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: belonging achieved not by blood or fleet, but by tending; the garden finally has its people.
